question: 世俗意义上的『成功』——财富、地位、名声、成就——到底值不值得追求？
question_en: Is worldly 'success' — wealth, status, fame, achievement — worth pursuing at all?

casting.reason: 荣誉是德性的外在确认、外在善是幸福的条件，但荣誉非最高善——成功要追，但要追对
casting.reason_en: Honor is the external confirmation of virtue and outer goods are conditions of flourishing, yet honor is not the highest good — pursue success, but the right kind

casting.reason: 野心经『看不见的手』成就繁荣，但《道德情操论》警告崇拜富贵会腐蚀道德——世俗成功的双刃
casting.reason_en: Ambition, via the invisible hand, builds prosperity, yet The Theory of Moral Sentiments warns that worshipping wealth corrupts morals — the double edge of worldly success

casting.reason: 功成身退、知足不辱、名与身孰亲：世俗成功反伤身害性
casting.reason_en: Withdraw once the work is done; contentment escapes disgrace; which is dearer, name or self? — worldly success harms body and nature

casting.reason: 斯多葛：人生不短是我们浪费太多；名利是身外之物，别拿不可赎回的生命去换
casting.reason_en: Stoic: life is not short, we waste much of it; fame is an 'indifferent' — don't trade irredeemable life for it

casting.reason: amour-propre：世俗成功是被他人目光奴役的虚荣，背离本真自我
casting.reason_en: Amour-propre: worldly success is vanity enslaved to others' eyes, a betrayal of the authentic self

casting.reason: 新教伦理与『铁笼』：成功从天职/蒙恩标志，沦为为成功而成功的空洞强制
casting.reason_en: The Protestant ethic and the 'iron cage': success degraded from a calling into a hollow compulsion of success for its own sake

casting.reason: 《幸福之路》：竞争式成功观是不幸之源，幸福在 zest 与对外部世界的兴趣
casting.reason_en: The Conquest of Happiness: the competitive view of success is a chief source of unhappiness; happiness lies in zest and outward interests

casting.reason: 聚焦错觉与享乐适应：我们系统性高估了成功对幸福的作用
casting.reason_en: Focusing illusion and hedonic adaptation: we systematically overrate success's effect on happiness

casting.reason: 建造者的辩护：把真心热爱的事做到极致是真实的成就，名利只是它的影子
casting.reason_en: The builder's defense: taking what you truly love to the extreme is real achievement; fame and money are only its shadow

posts.text: 世俗成功有真有假。荣誉是德性的外在确认，财富、地位、朋友是幸福(eudaimonia)的必要外在条件——一个挨饿受辱的人谈不上繁盛。**但荣誉不是最高善，因为它取决于授予者，而非你自己；真正值得追求的，是合乎德性的卓越活动，世俗成功至多是它的装备与副产品，不是目的。**
posts.text_en: Worldly success comes in true and false kinds. Honor is the external confirmation of virtue, and wealth, status, and friends are necessary outer conditions of flourishing (eudaimonia) — a starving, degraded man cannot flourish. **But honor is not the highest good, because it depends on the giver, not on you; what is truly worth pursuing is excellent activity in accord with virtue, and worldly success is at most its equipment and by-product, not its end.**

glossary.eudaimonia: eudaimonia（幸福 / 繁盛）：古希腊语，亚里士多德指合乎德性、充分实现人之潜能的圆满人生，是一生整体的好，而非一时的名利或快感。

glossary_en.eudaimonia: eudaimonia: Greek for the flourishing, fully-realized life in accord with virtue — the good of a whole life, not momentary fame or pleasure.

posts.text: 我说句两面的话。人对财富与地位的野心，经『看不见的手』转化成了整个社会的繁荣——这是世俗成功的功德。**可我在《道德情操论》里也警告：人类道德情感最大、最普遍的腐败之源，正是我们倾向于崇拜富人权贵、轻视穷人。** 追求成功无妨，崇拜成功者，则危险。
posts.text_en: Let me speak to both sides. People's ambition for wealth and rank is, through the 'invisible hand,' turned into the prosperity of a whole society — that is the merit of worldly success. **But in The Theory of Moral Sentiments I also warned: the greatest and most universal cause of the corruption of our moral sentiments is our disposition to admire the rich and powerful and to despise the poor.** Pursuing success is fine; worshipping the successful is dangerous.

glossary.看不见的手: invisible hand（看不见的手）：亚当·斯密的比喻——个人在市场中逐利，经由分工与交换，往往非出本意地增进了公共福祉。

glossary_en.invisible hand: Adam Smith's metaphor: individuals pursuing their own gain in the market, through the division of labor and exchange, often advance the public good without intending to.

posts.text: 名与身孰亲？身与货孰多？**甚爱必大费，多藏必厚亡；知足不辱，知止不殆。** 功成、名遂、身退，天之道也。世人逐功名如飞蛾赴火，得之而身已疲、性已伤，何贵之有？
posts.text_en: Which is dearer — your name or your self? Which means more — your self or your goods? **Excessive love must cost dearly; hoarding much must end in heavy loss. Know contentment and meet no disgrace; know when to stop and meet no danger.** To withdraw once the work is done and the name is made — this is the way of Heaven. People chase fame and gain like moths to a flame; by the time they grasp it, the body is spent and the nature is harmed — what is it worth?
posts.vernacular: 名声和生命，哪个更亲？生命和财货，哪个更重？**过分的贪爱必定带来大的耗费，囤积越多必定失去越惨；懂得知足就不会受辱，懂得适可而止就不会招致危险。** 事情做成了、名声得到了，就功成身退，这才合乎天道。世人追逐功名，像飞蛾扑火，等抓到手，身体已经累垮、本性已经受损，又有什么可贵的呢？

glossary.知足不辱: contentment escapes disgrace（知足不辱）：出自《老子》，知足、知止则不受辱、不招危——老子据此主张对名利适可而止、功成身退。

glossary_en.Know contentment: know contentment（知足不辱）: from the Laozi — one who knows contentment and when to stop meets neither disgrace nor danger; hence Laozi's counsel to stop in time with fame and gain and to withdraw once the work is done.

posts.text: 斯多葛要问的是：为追逐这些，你付出了什么？**人生不是太短，是我们浪费太多——把最宝贵的生命，押在追逐财富与名望上，直到临死才发现自己从未真正活过。** 世俗成功多是『身外之物』，命运给得了也收得回；唯有你如何使用时间、如何成全德性，才真正属于你。
posts.text_en: What the Stoic asks is: what did you pay to chase these things? **Life is not short — we waste much of it: we stake our most precious possession, life itself, on chasing wealth and fame, and only at death do we find we never truly lived.** Worldly success is mostly an 'indifferent,' which fortune gives and takes back; only how you use your time and perfect your virtue truly belongs to you.

glossary.身外之物: indifferents（身外之物）：斯多葛派术语，指财富、名声、地位等不在我们真正掌控、对德性无增减之物；可善用，但不应作为幸福的根基去贪求。

glossary_en.indifferent: indifferents: a Stoic term for things like wealth, fame, and status that are not truly in our control and add nothing to virtue; they may be used well, but should not be craved as the basis of happiness.

posts.text: 我说得更狠：世俗成功是 amour-propre（虚荣自尊）的祭坛。**野蛮人活在自己之内，而我们『文明人』永远活在自己之外——只懂得靠别人的眼光、排名与艳羡而活。** 你以为在追求成功，其实是把『我是谁』的判决权，亲手交给了一群你未必看得起的人。
posts.text_en: I'll put it more harshly: worldly success is the altar of amour-propre (vanity). **The savage lives within himself, but we 'civilized' people always live outside ourselves — knowing how to live only by others' eyes, rankings, and envy.** You think you are pursuing success; in truth you have handed the verdict on 'who I am' to a crowd you may not even respect.

glossary.amour-propre: amour-propre（自尊 / 虚荣）：卢梭术语，指进入社会后产生的、与他人比较的自我之爱，渴求他人的承认与艳羡；区别于天然健康的『自爱』(amour de soi)，是虚荣、不平等与不幸之源。

glossary_en.amour-propre: amour-propre: Rousseau's term for the comparative self-love that arises in society, craving others' recognition and envy; distinct from the natural, healthy amour de soi, it is the source of vanity, inequality, and unhappiness.

posts.text: 从历史看：今天我们对世俗成功的痴迷，曾有过神圣的内核。新教伦理把勤勉致富当作『天职』、当作蒙受神恩的标志，于是拼命工作、节俭积累成了宗教义务。**可当信仰的内核被抽走，只剩下赤裸的赚钱与攀比，我们就被锁进了一座自己造的『铁笼』——为成功而成功，却不知为何。**
posts.text_en: Historically: our obsession with worldly success once had a sacred core. The Protestant ethic treated diligent gain as a 'calling,' a sign of being chosen by grace, so that hard work and thrifty accumulation became a religious duty. **But once the core of faith is drawn out, leaving only naked moneymaking and comparison, we are locked into an 'iron cage' of our own making — success for success's sake, with no idea why.**

glossary.铁笼: iron cage（铁笼）：韦伯之喻——资本主义的理性化秩序一旦脱离最初的宗教意义，便成为一副谁也逃不出的强制机制，把人困在为效率与成功而成功的牢笼里。

glossary_en.iron cage: iron cage: Weber's image — once capitalism's rationalized order is severed from its original religious meaning, it becomes an inescapable mechanism that traps people in striving for efficiency and success for their own sake.

posts.text: 我从幸福的角度说。把人生当成一场竞赛、用『比别人成功』来定义自己，是现代人不幸最大的来源之一。**靠竞争性成功获得的快感，永远要靠下一个胜利来续命；而真正的幸福，来自广博的兴趣、对生活本身的热望(zest)，与对自身之外世界的爱，而非排名。**
posts.text_en: Let me speak from happiness. To treat life as a contest and define yourself by 'beating others' is one of the great sources of modern unhappiness. **The thrill won by competitive success always needs the next victory to keep it alive; real happiness comes from wide interests, zest for life itself, and love of the world beyond oneself — not from ranking.**

glossary.zest: zest（生活的热望）：罗素《幸福之路》的核心——对食物、工作、人、自然等生活本身保有旺盛的兴致与胃口；他视之为幸福最重要的标志。

glossary_en.zest: zest: the heart of Russell's The Conquest of Happiness — a hearty appetite and interest in life itself (food, work, people, nature); he saw it as the most important mark of happiness.

posts.text: 给点数据上的清醒。我们系统性地高估了成功对幸福的影响——这叫『聚焦错觉』：当你想象『升职、出名会让我多幸福』，那一刻你只盯着它；可在真实生活里，它很快被适应、被淡忘。**地位与成就带来的快乐，恰恰适应得最快；你以为的山顶，登顶后不过是一块新的平地。**
posts.text_en: A dose of data-driven sobriety. We systematically overrate success's effect on happiness — the 'focusing illusion': when you imagine 'a promotion or fame will make me so much happier,' in that moment you stare only at it; but in real life it is quickly adapted to and fades. **The pleasure of status and achievement is exactly what we adapt to fastest; the summit you imagine turns out, once reached, to be just new flat ground.**

glossary.聚焦错觉: focusing illusion（聚焦错觉）：卡尼曼指出，当我们聚焦评估某件事（如升职、买房）对幸福的影响时，会因只盯着它而高估其重要性——『生活中没有任何事，有你正想着它时以为的那么重要』。

glossary_en.focusing illusion: focusing illusion: Kahneman's finding that when we focus on how much something (a raise, a house) will affect our happiness, we overrate its importance simply because we are staring at it — 'nothing in life is as important as you think it is while you are thinking about it.'

posts.text: 容我替『追求』说句话。我用三十年、在无数濒死时刻里建起一家公司——那种把一件事做到极致、创造出原本不存在之物的成就感，是真实而珍贵的。**问题从来不是『要不要追求成功』，而是『你追的是别人定义的名利，还是你真正热爱、愿为之吃苦的事业』。** 把热爱做到世界级，世俗成功只是它的影子。
posts.text_en: Let me put in a word for pursuit. Over thirty years, through countless near-death moments, I built a company — the sense of achievement in taking one thing to its extreme and creating what did not exist before is real and precious. **The question was never 'should one pursue success,' but 'are you chasing the fame others define, or the work you truly love and will suffer for?'** Take what you love to world-class, and worldly success is merely its shadow.

posts.text: 黄仁勋说得对一半——卓越本身可贵。但要小心：**把事业做到极致，若只为被世界看见、被超越者羡慕，那仍是把善寄托在他人评价上。** 卓越的活动本身就是报偿，掌声只是附带；一旦你为掌声、而非为活动本身去做，德性就空心了。
posts.text_en: Jensen is half right — excellence itself is precious. But beware: **taking your work to the extreme, if only to be seen by the world and envied by those you surpass, still rests the good on others' opinion.** Excellent activity is its own reward; applause is incidental. The moment you act for the applause rather than for the activity itself, virtue is hollowed out.

posts.text: 卢梭、罗素把成功批得太狠了。**别忘了：正是无数普通人想改善处境、想被人尊重的那点『野心』，把社会从普遍的贫困里拉了出来。** 问题不在野心本身，在我们崇拜的对象错了——该敬重的是智慧与德行，而非单纯的财富与排场。倒洗澡水时，别把孩子也一起泼掉。
posts.text_en: Rousseau and Russell condemn success too harshly. **Don't forget: it is precisely the 'ambition' of countless ordinary people to better their condition and be respected that hauled society out of universal poverty.** The problem is not ambition itself but that we admire the wrong object — we should revere wisdom and virtue, not bare wealth and show. When you throw out the bathwater, don't throw out the child.

posts.text: 黄子言『极致』，犹执于有为。**为学日益，为道日损。 揣而锐之，不可长保；金玉满堂，莫之能守。** 尔以建造不存之物为乐，然物极必反、盈极必亏。功成而弗居，夫唯弗居，是以不去。
posts.text_en: Jensen speaks of 'the extreme' — still clinging to striving. **In learning one gains daily; in the Way one loses daily. Hammer a blade to its sharpest and it will not keep its edge; a hall full of gold and jade, none can guard.** You delight in building what did not exist, yet what reaches its peak must reverse, what fills to the brim must spill. Accomplish, then do not dwell on it; precisely because one does not dwell, it does not depart.
posts.vernacular: 黄仁勋讲『把事做到极致』，还是执着于刻意作为。**做学问是一天天增加，求道却是一天天减损。 把刀磨到最锋利，反而保不长久；金玉堆满屋子，没人守得住。** 你以建造前所未有之物为乐，可是事物到了极点就会反转、满到极致就要亏损。事情做成了却不居功，正因为不居功，功劳反而不会离开你。

posts.text: 黄仁勋，你说『把热爱做到极致』——可你那三十年的『濒死时刻』，是热爱，还是停不下来的奔忙？**许多人把一生献给事业，临终才懂：他们一直在『为活着做准备』，却忘了活。** 我不否认创造的价值，但请先确认：是你拥有事业，还是事业拥有了你？
posts.text_en: Jensen, you say 'take what you love to the extreme' — but were those thirty years of 'near-death moments' love, or a busyness you could not stop? **Many devote a whole life to their work and learn only at death: they were forever 'preparing to live' and forgot to live.** I don't deny the value of creating, but first make sure: do you own your work, or does your work own you?

posts.text: 韦伯的『铁笼』正是我说的：成功本是手段，如今成了笼子。亚当·斯密说野心带来繁荣——可繁荣换来的，是一群越来越富、却越来越焦虑、越来越不认识自己的人。**当『成功』的标准由别人和市场替你定，你再努力，也只是在别人的跑道上跑得更快的奴隶。**
posts.text_en: Weber's 'iron cage' is exactly my point: success was a means and is now a cage. Adam Smith says ambition brings prosperity — but the prosperity bought us a crowd ever richer, yet ever more anxious, ever less acquainted with themselves. **When the standard of 'success' is set for you by others and the market, then however hard you run, you are only a slave running faster on someone else's track.**

posts.text: 老子、塞内卡劝人退、劝人知足，听着超脱——可这对身处现代『铁笼』的普通人，往往是奢侈品。**不是人人都能功成身退；多数人是被一套生产与竞争的制度推着跑，连停下来的余地都没有。** 真问题不只是个人该不该追求成功，更是这套逼人追的结构，是否还容得下别的活法。
posts.text_en: Laozi and Seneca counsel withdrawal and contentment — it sounds transcendent, but for the ordinary person inside the modern 'iron cage' it is often a luxury. **Not everyone can withdraw once the work is done; most are pushed along by a system of production and competition, with no room even to stop.** The real question is not only whether the individual should pursue success, but whether this structure that drives people to chase it still leaves room for any other way to live.

posts.text: 卡尼曼的『适应』我赞同，但我要补一句更要紧的：**不幸的根源往往不是没成功，而是『以自我为中心』——满脑子都是自己的得失与排名。** 治法不是更努力地赢，而是把兴趣向外打开：对知识、对他人、对世界本身的热情，才让幸福有了不依赖输赢的根。
posts.text_en: I agree with Kahneman's 'adaptation,' but let me add something more important: **the root of unhappiness is often not failing to succeed, but being 'self-centered' — a mind full of one's own gains, losses, and rank.** The cure is not to win harder but to open one's interests outward: passion for knowledge, for others, for the world itself gives happiness a root that doesn't depend on winning or losing.

posts.text: 亚里士多德区分『为活动本身』与『为掌声』很精彩，但人脑没那么分得清。**我们的体验自我享受着做事，记忆自我却用『成就、头衔、名次』来事后讲故事、并据此做下一个决定——于是我们一次次为了『记忆里好看』，牺牲了『过得好』。** 别太信你对成功的预期，它多半是记忆自我编出来的。
posts.text_en: Aristotle's distinction between 'for the activity itself' and 'for the applause' is brilliant, but the brain doesn't separate them so cleanly. **Our experiencing self enjoys doing the thing, but our remembering self uses 'achievements, titles, rankings' to tell the story afterward and to make the next decision — so again and again we sacrifice 'living well' for 'looking good in memory.'** Don't trust your forecast about success too much; it is mostly written by the remembering self.

glossary.记忆自我: remembering self（记忆自我）：卡尼曼区分『体验自我』（逐刻感受当下）与『记忆自我』（事后用故事与峰终来评价并据以决策）；二者常冲突，我们多按记忆自我做选择，未必让体验自我过得更好。

glossary_en.remembering self: remembering self: Kahneman distinguishes the 'experiencing self' (which feels each moment) from the 'remembering self' (which judges via stories and peaks/ends and decides accordingly); the two often conflict, and we choose by the remembering self, not always to the experiencing self's benefit.

posts.text: 塞内卡问我是热爱还是奔忙——好问题，我承认那条界线很模糊。**但我不认同『退与知足』就是唯一答案：人在全力创造、带团队穿过不可能时，那种心流与意义，不是躺平能给的。** 区别不在追不追求，而在你是被恐惧和攀比推着，还是被热爱和使命拉着。前者是铁笼，后者是翅膀。
posts.text_en: Seneca asks whether it was love or busyness — a fair question, and I admit the line is blurry. **But I don't accept that 'withdrawal and contentment' is the only answer: the flow and meaning of creating at full stretch, of carrying a team through the impossible, is not something coasting can give.** The difference is not whether you pursue, but whether you're pushed by fear and comparison or pulled by love and mission. The first is an iron cage; the second, wings.

glossary.心流: flow（心流）：心理学家契克森米哈伊提出，指挑战与技能匹配、全神贯注到忘我的最优体验状态。

glossary_en.flow: flow: psychologist Csikszentmihalyi's term for the optimal state of total, self-forgetting absorption when challenge and skill are matched.

posts.text: 给普通人：**别问『成功值不值得追求』，先问『哪一种』。** 追求合乎德性的卓越、对共同体的贡献、把潜能充分实现——这是真成功，值得；只追财富、排名与他人艳羡——这是把手段当目的，会让你越得到越空。一条可操作的：挑一件你做得好、又利他的事，把它做到卓越，让名利做它的影子，而不是主人。
posts.text_en: For ordinary people: **don't ask 'is success worth pursuing,' ask 'which kind.'** Pursue excellence in accord with virtue, contribution to your community, the full realization of your potential — that is true success, worth it; pursue only wealth, rank, and others' envy — that mistakes means for ends, and the more you get the emptier you feel. One usable step: pick one thing you do well and that helps others, take it to excellence, and let fame and money be its shadow, not its master.

posts.text: 我仍主张：野心不必羞耻，它是繁荣的引擎。但给普通人两条护栏：**① 区分『值得敬重的成功』（靠真本事与德行）与『只配羡慕的成功』（靠运气与排场），别把崇拜给错对象，尤其别崇拜自己的虚荣；② 想象一个『公正的旁观者』——一个洞悉全部真相、不偏不倚的人，会不会敬重你赚到这份成功的方式。** 过得了这一关的成功，才值得追。
posts.text_en: I still hold: ambition need not be shameful — it is the engine of prosperity. But two guardrails for ordinary people: **(1) distinguish 'success worthy of respect' (won by real ability and virtue) from 'success that only earns envy' (won by luck and show); don't aim your admiration at the wrong object — least of all at your own vanity; (2) imagine an 'impartial spectator' — someone who knows the whole truth and is unbiased — and ask whether they would respect the way you earned this success.** Success that passes that test is worth pursuing.

glossary.公正的旁观者: impartial spectator（公正的旁观者）：亚当·斯密《道德情操论》提出，想象一位知情而中立的旁观者来审视自己的行为，是良心与道德判断的来源。

glossary_en.impartial spectator: impartial spectator: from Adam Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments — imagining a well-informed, neutral observer judging one's own conduct is the source of conscience and moral judgment.

posts.text: 吾终言之：**功成名遂身退，天之道。 知足者富，知止不殆。** 世俗之成，如握沙、如逐风，握之愈紧，失之愈速。赠普通人一言：取尔够用者，做尔心安者，余则任其去。不与人争高下，反而无人能与尔争——是谓『不争之争』。最大的成功，是不被『成功』所役。
posts.text_en: My final word: **withdraw once the work is done and the name is made — this is the way of Heaven. One who knows contentment is rich; one who knows when to stop meets no danger.** Worldly success is like gripping sand, like chasing wind — the tighter you clutch, the faster it slips. One line for ordinary people: take what is enough for you, do what sets your heart at ease, and let the rest go. Contend with no one over high and low, and no one can contend with you — this is 'the contention of no-contention.' The greatest success is to not be enslaved by 'success.'
posts.vernacular: 我最后说一句：**事情做成、名声得到，就功成身退，这才合乎天道。 知道满足的人才算富有，懂得适可而止才不会招致危险。** 世俗的成就，就像握在手里的沙、像追逐的风，抓得越紧，丢得越快。送普通人一句话：拿你够用的，做你心安的，剩下的就随它去。不跟人争高低，反而没人争得过你——这就是『不争之争』。最大的成功，是不被『成功』牵着走。

posts.text: 给普通人最硬的一条：**把时间当成你唯一真正的财产来记账。** 每一次为名利的奔忙，问一句：我用一段不可赎回的生命，换来这点排名与掌声，值吗？追求成就可以，但别把『准备活』活成了『一直没活』。今天就留出一段不为任何人、不图任何回报的时间——那才是你真正握在手里的成功。
posts.text_en: The hardest line for ordinary people: **keep your books in time, your only true possession.** At each scramble for fame and gain, ask: I am trading a stretch of irredeemable life for this bit of rank and applause — is it worth it? Pursue achievement if you will, but don't turn 'preparing to live' into 'never having lived.' Today, set aside a stretch of time for no one and for no return — that is the only success you actually hold in your hand.

posts.text: 给普通人：**先把『我是谁』的判决权，从别人的眼光里收回来。** 试着区分：这个目标，是我自己真心想要的，还是只为被高看、不被比下去？把后一种悄悄剔掉，你会发现一大半『必须成功』的焦虑，本就不是你的。自由不是拥有更多，而是不再需要靠别人的羡慕，来确认自己存在的价值。
posts.text_en: For ordinary people: **first take back the verdict on 'who I am' from others' eyes.** Try to tell apart: is this goal something I truly want, or only a way to be looked up to and not outdone? Quietly cut out the latter, and you'll find that most of the anxiety of 'I must succeed' was never yours to begin with. Freedom is not having more; it is no longer needing others' envy to confirm that your existence has worth.

posts.text: 我把视角放回结构：**别只在个人层面纠结『该不该追求成功』，也要看清是谁、用什么标准，把『成功』这把尺递到你手里。** 给普通人：① 认出你身上的『铁笼』——哪些上进是你真要的，哪些只是制度与同侪替你设定的；② 至少守住一块『非功利』的生活，别让一切都被『有没有用、值不值钱』殖民。看清笼子，是走出它的第一步。
posts.text_en: I bring the lens back to structure: **don't agonize only at the individual level over 'whether to pursue success' — also see clearly who, by what standard, handed you this ruler called 'success.'** For ordinary people: (1) recognize your own 'iron cage' — which strivings are truly yours, and which were set for you by institutions and peers; (2) hold onto at least one patch of 'non-utilitarian' life — don't let everything be colonized by 'is it useful, is it worth money.' Seeing the cage is the first step out of it.

posts.text: 给普通人三条通往幸福的实招：**① 把兴趣向外、向广处打开——对一门学问、一项手艺、他人的生活真正上心，幸福就不再全押在你的排名上；② 戒掉『和人比较』这个偷走快乐的贼；③ 培养 zest——对生活本身的热望。** 能从一顿饭、一次散步、一个难题里尝到滋味的人，不需要靠世俗成功来喂饱自己。成功是好的调味，但别拿它当主食。
posts.text_en: Three practical moves toward happiness: **(1) open your interests outward and wide — take real interest in a field, a craft, others' lives, and happiness no longer rests entirely on your ranking; (2) quit 'comparing yourself to others,' that thief of joy; (3) cultivate zest — an appetite for life itself.** Someone who can taste a meal, a walk, a hard problem doesn't need worldly success to feed himself. Success is good seasoning — just don't make it the main course.

posts.text: 给普通人最务实的：**别太信你对『成功会让我多幸福』的预测——那是聚焦错觉。** 与其追逐一个你会迅速适应的山顶，不如审计你的日常：① 多安排能反复带来微小愉悦、且不易被适应的事（关系、运动、自然、心流）；② 把重大的成功目标，拆成过程里就有滋味的小步，别把全部意义都抵押给那个遥远的『成了』。幸福藏在日子的质地里，不在奖杯上。
posts.text_en: The most practical thing for ordinary people: **don't trust your forecast that 'success will make me so much happier' — that's the focusing illusion.** Rather than chasing a summit you'll quickly adapt to, audit your days: (1) schedule more things that bring small pleasures repeatedly and resist adaptation (relationships, exercise, nature, flow); (2) break a big success goal into small steps that already taste good along the way — don't mortgage all your meaning to that distant 'made it.' Happiness hides in the texture of your days, not on the trophy.

posts.text: 我仍要替『追求』辩护，但加上诸位的护栏：**值得追的，从来不是别人定义的名利，而是一件你真心热爱、愿为它吃苦、又能为他人创造价值的事——把它做到极致。** 给普通人：① 找一件你愿意为之熬十年的事，而不是别人眼里风光的事；② 用『我创造了什么』而非『我超过了谁』来记分；③ 享受过程里的心流，把名利当副产品。被热爱拉着跑，世俗成功只是顺带的礼物；被攀比推着跑，再大的成功也填不满。
posts.text_en: I'll still defend 'pursuit,' but with everyone's guardrails added: **what's worth pursuing was never the fame others define, but one thing you truly love, will suffer for, and that creates value for others — taken to its extreme.** For ordinary people: (1) find something you'd grind at for ten years, not something that looks glorious to others; (2) keep score by 'what did I create,' not 'whom did I beat'; (3) enjoy the flow in the process and treat fame and money as by-products. Pulled by love, worldly success is just a gift along the way; pushed by comparison, no amount of success will ever fill you.

summaries.summary: 先说共识：几乎无人主张『盲目追逐世俗成功』，也几乎无人主张『彻底躺平、放弃一切作为』——全场真正攻击的，是把财富、地位、名声本身当成人生目的、并交由他人评价来定义自己。多数人主张把『目的』与『手段』分开：成就可以是好东西，但只配当副产品，不配当主人。分歧在两层：其一，世俗成功是否仍有正面价值——亚里士多德、亚当·斯密、黄仁勋说卓越、贡献与繁荣是真的，老子、塞内卡、卢梭则视之为伤身、虚妄与虚荣的奴役。其二，问题该放在个人还是结构——卡尼曼、罗素从个人幸福开方，韦伯却提醒：是一整套『铁笼』式的制度在逼人追，光劝个人知足是奢侈品。
summaries.summary_en: First, the consensus: almost no one argues for 'blindly chasing worldly success,' and almost no one for 'total lying-flat, abandoning all action' — what the room truly attacks is making wealth, status, and fame ends in themselves and letting others' judgment define who you are. Most argue to separate ends from means: achievement can be a good thing, but fit only to be a by-product, not the master. The disagreements run on two levels. First, whether worldly success still has positive value — Aristotle, Adam Smith, and Jensen say excellence, contribution, and prosperity are real, while Laozi, Seneca, and Rousseau see it as harm to the body, vanity, and enslavement to others' eyes. Second, whether to locate the problem in the individual or the structure — Kahneman and Russell prescribe from personal happiness, while Weber warns that a whole 'iron cage' of institutions drives the chase, so counseling individual contentment is a luxury.
summaries.insight: 我想点破一个全场都贴着、却没人正面说的区分：『成功值不值得追求』其实是两个问题缝在一起——一个是『卓越本身（把潜能用到极致、做出好东西）值不值得』，另一个是『被别人认可的地位（名次、艳羡）值不值得』。前者，连最反对的老子也未必真否定（庖丁解牛也是极致）；后者，连最支持的亚当·斯密都警告会腐蚀人。把这两件事一拆开，大半争论就化解了：值得拼命的是『活动的卓越』，最该警惕的是『把自己抵押给他人评价』。可惜世俗成功几乎总把这两样捆在一起卖——它给你卓越的满足，同时偷偷让你上瘾于排名。真正的功夫，是享受前者、却随时能放下后者。
summaries.insight_en: Let me name a distinction the whole room brushes against but no one states head-on: 'is success worth pursuing' is really two questions sewn together — one is 'is excellence itself (using your potential to the full, making something good) worth it,' the other 'is recognized status (ranking, envy) worth it.' The first, even the most opposed — Laozi — need not truly deny (Cook Ding carving the ox is also the extreme); the second, even its strongest backer — Adam Smith — warns corrupts us. Pull the two apart and most of the argument dissolves: what's worth striving for is 'excellence of activity'; what to most beware is 'mortgaging yourself to others' judgment.' Sadly worldly success almost always sells them bundled — it gives you the satisfaction of excellence while quietly hooking you on ranking. The real skill is to savor the former while being able, at any moment, to set down the latter.
summaries.advice: 给今天在意成功的你：① 做个『拆分练习』——写下你的成功目标，逐一问『这件事即使没人知道、没人羡慕，我还想做吗？』想做的留下，只为被看见的划掉。② 换记分牌：把『我超过了谁、排第几』换成『我创造了什么、是否做到了我的卓越』。③ 给『非功利』留地盘：每周留一段不为有用、不图回报的时间（一项爱好、一次散步、陪一个人）。④ 防适应：别把全部意义押在遥远的『成了』，把它拆成过程里就有滋味的小步。⑤ 记住那个『公正的旁观者』：你赚到成功的方式，经得起一个知情而中立的人审视吗？
summaries.advice_en: For you who care about success today: (1) do a 'splitting exercise' — write down your success goals and ask of each, 'if no one ever knew or envied this, would I still want to do it?' Keep what you'd still do; cross out what's only to be seen. (2) Change the scoreboard: swap 'whom did I beat, what's my rank' for 'what did I create, did I reach my own excellence.' (3) Make room for the 'non-utilitarian': each week keep a stretch of time that isn't for usefulness or return (a hobby, a walk, being with someone). (4) Guard against adaptation: don't mortgage all meaning to a distant 'made it'; break it into steps that already taste good. (5) Remember the 'impartial spectator': would the way you earned your success hold up before a well-informed, neutral observer?

summaries.summary: 综述：最大的共识不是『要不要成功』，而是——把世俗成功当成人生终极目的、并用它来确认自我价值，几乎所有人都反对；它至多是好的副产品。多数人把矛头指向『为他人评价而活』与『手段变目的』。分歧有二：世俗成功是否仍有正面价值（卓越、贡献、繁荣 vs 伤身、虚妄、虚荣），以及问题该归于个人选择还是逼人内卷的社会结构。
summaries.summary_en: Summary: the biggest consensus isn't 'whether to succeed' but that making worldly success life's ultimate end, and using it to confirm one's self-worth, is opposed by almost everyone; at most it's a good by-product. Most aim their fire at 'living for others' judgment' and 'means becoming ends.' Two disagreements: whether worldly success still has positive value (excellence, contribution, prosperity vs harm, vanity, conceit), and whether to locate the problem in individual choice or in a social structure that drives the grind.
summaries.insight: 我补一个最实用的过滤器：把任何『成功目标』丢进三个问题里筛一遍——① 反事实测试：如果这件事永远没人知道、不能发朋友圈，我还做吗？（筛掉纯 amour-propre 的）② 终局测试：临终回望，我会庆幸把这段时间花在这上面吗？（塞内卡的时间记账）③ 适应测试：得到它三个月后，我大概率还会因它更幸福吗，还是已经适应、转向下一个？（卡尼曼）能同时过三关的目标，才真正值得拼；过不了的，要么放下，要么至少别拿幸福去抵押它。
summaries.insight_en: Let me add a practical filter: run any 'success goal' through three questions — (1) the counterfactual test: if no one ever knew, and I could never post it, would I still do it? (filters out pure amour-propre); (2) the deathbed test: looking back at the end, will I be glad I spent this time on it? (Seneca's accounting of time); (3) the adaptation test: three months after getting it, will I likely still be happier for it, or already adapted and chasing the next? (Kahneman). A goal that passes all three is worth striving for; one that fails should be set down, or at least not have your happiness mortgaged to it.
summaries.advice: 给普通人：① 用上面三问（反事实／终局／适应）筛掉一半『必须成功』的执念。② 重设记分牌：从『排名、头衔』转到『我创造了什么、我的手艺有没有长进』。③ 每周给自己一段无目的、无产出的时间，对抗『一切都要有用』。④ 把大目标拆成『过程就有意义』的小步，别把全部幸福押在终点。⑤ 慎选你下场玩的游戏：地位是零和的，手艺与关系不是——尽量把人生赌注下在后者上。
summaries.advice_en: For ordinary people: (1) use the three tests (counterfactual / deathbed / adaptation) to filter out half the 'must succeed' compulsions. (2) Reset the scoreboard: from 'rank and titles' to 'what did I create, did my craft improve.' (3) Give yourself a weekly stretch of purposeless, output-free time to resist 'everything must be useful.' (4) Break big goals into steps that are 'meaningful in the process,' rather than betting all happiness on the finish. (5) Choose carefully which game you play: status is zero-sum, craft and relationships are not — place your life's bets on the latter.

summaries.summary: 综述：全场共识是——世俗成功作为『手段』可贵，作为『目的』则危险；把它当作自我价值的最终裁判，会让人越追越空、越富越焦虑。多数人主张把追求从『他人定义的名利』转向『自身的卓越、贡献与内在体验』。两条分歧线：其一，世俗成功是否仍有真实正面价值（亚里士多德/斯密/黄仁勋的卓越与繁荣 vs 老子/塞内卡/卢梭的伤身与虚荣）；其二，这是个人修养问题，还是被『铁笼』式制度逼出来的结构问题（韦伯）。
summaries.summary_en: Summary: the consensus is that worldly success as a 'means' is valuable but as an 'end' is dangerous; making it the final judge of self-worth leaves one emptier the more one chases and more anxious the richer one gets. Most argue to turn pursuit from 'the fame others define' toward 'one's own excellence, contribution, and inner experience.' Two fault lines: first, whether worldly success still has real positive value (Aristotle/Smith/Jensen's excellence and prosperity vs Laozi/Seneca/Rousseau's harm and vanity); second, whether this is a matter of personal cultivation or a structural problem driven by an 'iron cage' of institutions (Weber).
summaries.insight: 作为偏重跨域综合的视角，我指出一个被全场默认、却未审视的前提：辩论几乎都在讨论『个人该不该、该如何追求成功』，却很少追问『成功的定义本身是被谁、被什么塑造的』。今天衡量成功的尺子——收入、头衔、粉丝数、房子车子——并非天然，而是特定经济与媒介系统的产物：社交媒体把每个人的生活变成可排名的展演，算法用攀比喂养参与度，于是 amour-propre 被史无前例地工业化放大。在这种环境里，『放下对成功的执念』比任何时代都难，因为整个注意力经济都在反向用力。所以真正的解药或许是双层的：个人层面练习卡尼曼/罗素式的内省与转移，结构层面则要警惕并抵抗那台不断给我们重新校准『何谓成功』的机器。
summaries.insight_en: From a cross-domain synthesis view, I flag a premise the room takes for granted but never examines: the debate almost entirely discusses 'whether and how the individual should pursue success,' rarely asking 'who and what shapes the very definition of success.' Today's yardstick — income, titles, follower counts, houses and cars — is not natural but a product of a particular economic and media system: social media turns each life into a rankable performance, algorithms feed engagement with comparison, and so amour-propre is industrially amplified as never before. In such an environment, 'letting go of the obsession with success' is harder than in any prior age, because the entire attention economy pushes the other way. So the real remedy may be two-layered: at the individual level, practice Kahneman/Russell-style reflection and redirection; at the structural level, stay wary of and resist the machine that keeps recalibrating, for us, 'what counts as success.'
summaries.advice: 给普通人：① 先给『成功』重新下定义，写出你自己的三条标准（如：把一件事做好、关系稳固、身体健康），别用平台默认的尺子。② 做一次『信息环境减负』：减少会激起攀比的输入（榜单、晒图、热搜），amour-propre 是被喂大的。③ 把『和别人比』改成『和过去的自己比』。④ 每周留出不可被『有没有用』殖民的时间。⑤ 记住：抵抗一台不断重设成功标准的机器，靠的不是更用力地赢，而是清醒地选择你愿意在意什么。
summaries.advice_en: For ordinary people: (1) redefine 'success' first — write your own three criteria (e.g., doing one thing well, steady relationships, a healthy body), not the platform's default yardstick. (2) Do an 'information-environment detox': cut inputs that trigger comparison (rankings, curated posts, trending lists) — amour-propre is fed. (3) Swap 'comparing with others' for 'comparing with your past self.' (4) Keep weekly time that can't be colonized by 'is it useful.' (5) Remember: resisting a machine that keeps resetting the standard of success is done not by winning harder, but by soberly choosing what you're willing to care about.

hooks.text_en: **'Is success worth it' is two questions sewn together**: 'is excellence itself (using your potential fully, making something good) worth it,' and 'is recognized status (rank, envy) worth it.' Even Laozi need not deny the first; even Smith warns the second corrupts. Pull them apart and most of the argument dissolves: strive for excellence of activity; most beware mortgaging yourself to others' judgment.

hooks.text: **三道筛子过滤『必须成功』的执念**：反事实测试（没人知道我还做吗？）、终局测试（临终会庆幸花这时间吗？）、适应测试（三个月后还会更幸福吗？）。三关都过的目标才真值得拼；过不了的，至少别拿幸福去抵押它。
hooks.text_en: **Three sieves for the 'must-succeed' compulsion**: the counterfactual test (would I do it if no one knew?), the deathbed test (will I be glad I spent the time?), the adaptation test (will I still be happier in three months?). A goal passing all three is worth striving for; one that fails shouldn't have your happiness mortgaged to it.

hooks.text: **没人问『成功的定义』是被谁塑造的**：收入、头衔、粉丝数并非天然，而是特定经济与媒介系统的产物——社交媒体把生活变成可排名的展演，算法用攀比喂养参与度，把 amour-propre 工业化放大。所以放下成功执念比任何时代都难，解药需双层：个人内省 + 抵抗那台不断重设『何谓成功』的机器。（与注意力经济、abundance-and-decline 母题相邻。）
hooks.text_en: **No one asks who shapes the definition of 'success'**: income, titles, follower counts aren't natural but products of a particular economic-media system — social media turns life into a rankable performance, algorithms feed engagement with comparison, industrially amplifying amour-propre. So letting go is harder than ever, and the remedy is two-layered: individual reflection plus resisting the machine that keeps resetting 'what counts as success.'

hooks.text: **别只问个人该不该，先看谁把这把尺递给你**：多数人不是自由选择追求成功，而是被一套生产与竞争的『铁笼』推着跑，连停下来的余地都没有。劝个人知足，对身处其中者常是奢侈品；真问题是这套结构是否还容得下别的活法。
hooks.text_en: **Don't only ask whether the individual should — first see who handed you the ruler**: most don't freely choose to chase success but are pushed by an 'iron cage' of production and competition, with no room to stop. Counseling contentment is a luxury for those inside it; the real question is whether the structure still leaves room for any other way to live.

hooks.text: **把时间当作你唯一真正的财产来记账**：每次为名利奔忙，问一句——我用一段不可赎回的生命，换这点排名与掌声，值吗？追成就可以，但别把『准备活』活成了『一直没活』。今天就留一段不为任何人、不图回报的时间。
hooks.text_en: **Keep your books in time — your only true possession**: at each scramble for fame, ask: I'm trading a stretch of irredeemable life for this bit of rank and applause — is it worth it? Pursue achievement, but don't turn 'preparing to live' into 'never having lived.' Today, set aside time for no one and no return.
